name: sdk
purpose: WAVE is media infrastructure for the agentic internet: one call shape moves live and on-demand media across every transport, and both kinds of user, people and agents, discover it, call it, and pay for it per call. This SDK is the TypeScript client for that call shape: API modules covering streaming, production, device management, analytics, content, and monetization behind a single `Wave` client. Most modules are SDK-side TypeScript surface only; see capability statuses for what has a live backend today.

capabilities.does: Live stream lifecycle, protocols, recordings, viewer metrics via `wave.pipeline`
Video clips, exports, AI highlights via `wave.clips`
Video editing, tracks, transitions, effects via `wave.editor`
Text-to-speech via `wave.voice.synthesize()`; voice-clone methods exist as SDK client surface but are not backed by the wave-voice product yet
Multi-camera production, scenes, transitions, graphics, audio mixing via `wave.studio` (SDK TypeScript surface; no fleet backend yet)
Virtual Device Bridge (NDI/ONVIF/VISCA/Dante to USB UVC/UAC) via `wave.prism` (SDK TypeScript surface; no fleet backend yet)
Desktop Node fleet management, health, commands via `wave.fleet` (SDK TypeScript surface; no fleet backend yet)
AI auto-directing (Autopilot), suggestions, overrides via `wave.ghost` (SDK TypeScript surface; no fleet backend yet)
Multi-region failover, replication, topology via `wave.mesh` (SDK TypeScript surface; no fleet backend yet)
Analytics, BI dashboards, revenue metrics via `wave.pulse` (SDK TypeScript surface; no fleet backend yet)
Recording storage, VOD, archive policies via `wave.vault` (SDK TypeScript surface; no fleet backend yet)
Monetization, subscriptions, tips, payouts via `wave.creator` (SDK TypeScript surface; no fleet backend yet)
Telephony bridging via `wave.phone` — core features are planned in the fleet SSOT, not yet shipped
Podcast publishing/distribution via `wave.podcast` — core features are planned in the fleet SSOT, not yet shipped

Agent routing (route/pool) and an OpenAI-compatible proxy for LLM/agent traffic, shipped at the WAVE gateway; reachable from the SDK today via the base `WaveClient` request methods (no dedicated wrapper module yet)

x402 and MPP card-rail agent payments with scope-gate and settlement-guard, shipped at the WAVE gateway; reachable from the SDK today via the base `WaveClient` request methods (no dedicated wrapper module yet)

claims.text: The npm package is published as @wave-av/sdk
42 independently-importable API module subpaths are declared under package.json exports, plus the package root
A single `Wave` client class in src/index.ts composes every API module as a readonly property
Each API module is independently importable via a package.json subpath export (e.g. @wave-av/sdk/pipeline)
The base WaveClient exposes a generic protected request() method that any endpoint — including gateway/dispatch routes without a dedicated wrapper module — can be reached through
wave.voice.synthesize() implements text-to-speech; the SDK also declares cloneVoice() client methods that are not backed by the wave-voice product
Takes zod ^3.22.0 as a peer dependency for runtime validation
